     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space, and their conditional-linearity levels are
    12	established below; the line-point distributions they induce are analysed in
    13	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    32	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    34	`def:ld-game` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, with paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    37	-/
    38	structure LdParams where
    39	  q : ℕ
    40	  m : ℕ
    41	  d : ℕ
    42	  k : ℕ
    43	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    44	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    45	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    46	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    47	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    48	
    49	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    50	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    51	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    52	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    53	
    54	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    55	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    56	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    60	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    61	
    62	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    63	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    64	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    66	-/
    67	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    68	
    69	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    72	-/
    73	inductive LdType where
    74	  | point
    75	  | aline
    76	  | dline
    77	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    78	
    79	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    82	-/
    83	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    84	
    85	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    88	-/
    89	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    90	
    91	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   101	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   102	
   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   105	-/
   106	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   107	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   108	
   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   177	
   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   180	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   181	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   182	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   183	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   184	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   185	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}
   186	
   187	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   188	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   189	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   190	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P)
   191	
   192	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the direction
   193	coordinates of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   194	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   195	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P)
   196	
   197	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   198	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   199	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   200	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   201	  toFun x := fun i =>
   202	    match i with
   203	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   204	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   205	    | .inr _ => 0
   206	  map_add' x y := by
   207	    funext i
   208	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   209	  map_smul' c x := by
   210	    funext i
   211	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   212	
   213	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   214	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   215	other coordinate. -/
   216	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   217	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   218	  toFun x := fun i =>
   219	    match i with
   220	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   221	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   222	    | .inr _ => 0
   223	  map_add' x y := by
   224	    funext i
   225	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   226	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   227	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   228	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   229	      rfl
   230	    · simp
   231	    · simp
   232	  map_smul' c x := by
   233	    funext i
   234	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   235	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   237	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   238	      rfl
   239	    · simp
   240	    · simp
   241	
   242	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   243	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   244	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   245	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   246	  toFun x := fun k =>
   247	    match k with
   248	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   249	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   250	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   251	  map_add' x y := by
   252	    funext k
   253	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   254	    · simp
   255	    · simp
   256	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   257	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   258	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   259	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   260	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   261	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   262	        rfl
   263	  map_smul' c x := by
   264	    funext k
   265	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   266	    · simp
   267	    · simp
   268	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   269	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   270	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   271	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   272	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   273	        rfl
   274	
   275	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the shared-scalar map vanishes
   276	outside the scalar register. -/
   277	private theorem ldSeedLinear_supported (P : LdParams) :
   278	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldSeedRegister P →
   279	      ldSeedLinear P x i = 0 := by
   280	  intro x i hi
   281	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   282	  · rfl
   283	  · cases u
   284	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_singleton_self _) hi
   285	  · rfl
   286	
   287	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the canonical-representative map
   288	vanishes outside the point register. -/
   289	private theorem ldPointCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   290	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (i : LdIndex P), i ∉ ldPointRegister P →
   291	      ldPointCLLinear P v x i = 0 := by
   292	  intro x i hi
   293	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   294	  · exact absurd (Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_univ j)) hi
   295	  · rfl
   296	  · rfl
   297	
   298	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the prefix-zeroing map vanishes
   299	outside the direction register. -/
   300	private theorem ldDirectionCLLinear_supported (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   301	    ∀ (x : LdSpace P) (k : LdIndex P), k ∉ ldDirectionRegister P →
   302	      ldDirectionCLLinear P i x k = 0 := by
   303	  intro x k hk

   362	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a two-level representation of the
   363	affine-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   364	private noncomputable def ldALineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   365	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 2 :=
   366	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   367	    fun y =>
   368	      .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   369	        (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y))))
   370	        (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   371	        fun _ => .zero
   372	
   373	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a three-level representation of the
   374	diagonal-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   375	private noncomputable def ldDLineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   376	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 3 :=
   377	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   378	    fun y =>
   379	      .succ (ldDirectionRegister P)
   380	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))
   381	        (ldDirectionCLLinear_supported P _)
   382	        fun w =>
   383	          .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   384	            (ldPointCLLinear P (LdSpace.direction w))
   385	            (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   386	            fun _ => .zero
   387	
   388	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is
   389	`lem:ld-aline-level`, the level-2 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   390	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:61-71`, paper
   391	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   392	-/
   393	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   394	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   395	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   396	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   397	  funext x
   398	  have hseed :
   399	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   400	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   401	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   402	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   403	  have hval :
   404	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   405	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   406	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   407	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   408	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   409	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   410	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   411	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   412	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   413	    rw [hseed]
   414	  rw [hval]
   415	  funext i
   416	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   417	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   418	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   419	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   420	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   421	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   422	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   423	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   424	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   425	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   426	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   427	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]
   428	
   429	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is
   430	`lem:ld-dline-level`, the level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   431	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:73-83`, paper origin
   432	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   433	-/
   434	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   435	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by

     5	/-!
     6	# Lines, bounded line polynomials, and line-point distributions
     7	
     8	This file provides the seed-bearing line descriptions and coefficient-list
     9	polynomials shared by the observable and combining chapters. It also realizes
    10	the line-point distribution directly from the conditionally linear sampler.
    11	Over a finite coefficient field, bounded individual-degree multivariate
    12	polynomials form a finite outcome set for the associated measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The line and bounded-polynomial definitions are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-86`, with source origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. The
    19	line-point sampler is `def:line-point-dist` in blueprint chapter 13, from
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29

    31	
    32	/-- A formalization-only identity used to construct canonical line
    33	descriptions: applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has
    34	the same effect as applying it once. -/
    35	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    36	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    37	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    38	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    39	
    40	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    41	inductive LineKind where
    42	  | axis
    43	  | diagonal
    44	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    45	
    46	/-- A seed-bearing line description for `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    47	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper
    48	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
    49	
    50	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    51	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    52	Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
    54	corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Multivariate polynomials in `m` variables whose total degree is at most
   110	`d`. This is the class `deg_d` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, blueprint
   111	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-48`, paper
   112	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-52`. -/
   113	abbrev TotalDegreePoly (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :=
   114	  {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K // p.totalDegree ≤ d}
   115	
   116	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   117	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   118	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   119	
   120	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   121	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   122	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   123	  fun i =>
   124	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   125	
   126	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   127	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   128	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   129	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   130	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   131	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   132	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   133	
   134	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   135	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   136	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   138	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   139	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   140	  classical
   141	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   142	    some (Classical.choose h)
   143	  else none
   144	
   145	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   147	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   151	
   152	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   153	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   154	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   156	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   157	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   158	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   159	      intro j hj
   160	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   161	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   162	
   163	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   164	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   165	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   171	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   172	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   173	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   174	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   175	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   176	
   177	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   178	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   179	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   180	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   181	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   182	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   183	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   184	
   185	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   186	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   187	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   188	  sorry
   189	
   190	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   191	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   192	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   193	  sorry
   194	
   195	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   196	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   197	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   198	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   199	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   200	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   201

     7	/-!
     8	# Completeness of the Pauli basis test
     9	
    10	This file presents the Pauli basis test as a symmetric game and states its
    11	value-one SPCC completeness theorem.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source statement is `lem:pauli-completeness` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:390-395`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1229-1421`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	/-- The Pauli question sampler equals the typed conditionally linear distribution
    25	on the Pauli type graph from `def:typed-cl-distributions`; blueprint
    26	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:624-629`,
    27	paper `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    28	theorem pauliQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    29	    pauliQuestionDistribution P =
    30	      typedCLDistribution pauliEdges (by
    31	        refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.point .X), ?_⟩
    32	        simp [pauliEdges]) (pauliCL P) (pauliCL P) := by
    33	  sorry
    34	
    35	/-- Symmetry of the Pauli question distribution in the symmetric game appearing
    36	in `lem:pauli-completeness`. -/
    37	theorem pauliQuestionDistribution_symm (P : AdmissibleParams)
    38	    (x y : PauliQuestion P) :
    39	    (pauliQuestionDistribution P).weight (x, y) =
    40	      (pauliQuestionDistribution P).weight (y, x) := by
    41	  sorry
    42	
    43	/-- Symmetry of the Pauli decision predicate in the symmetric game appearing in
    44	`lem:pauli-completeness`. -/
    45	theorem pauliWinPredicate_symm (P : AdmissibleParams)
    46	    (x y : PauliQuestion P) (a b : PauliAnswer P) :
    47	    pauliWinPredicate P x y a b = pauliWinPredicate P y x b a := by
    48	  sorry
    49	
    50	/-- The symmetric presentation of the Pauli basis test. The field and basis
    51	are those fixed by `P.model`; no additional model is quantified. -/
    52	noncomputable def pauliBasisTestSymm (P : AdmissibleParams) : SymmetricGame where
    53	  Question := PauliQuestion P
    54	  Answer := PauliAnswer P
    55	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
    56	  μ_prob := (pauliBasisTest P).μ_prob
    57	  μ_symm := pauliQuestionDistribution_symm P
    58	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
    59	  decide_symm := pauliWinPredicate_symm P
    60	
    61	/-- The symmetric presentation has the Pauli basis test as its
    62	underlying game. -/
    63	theorem pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    64	    (pauliBasisTestSymm P).toGame = pauliBasisTest P := by
    65	  rfl
    66	
    67	/-- `lem:pauli-completeness`: every admissible Pauli basis test has a
    68	value-one SPCC strategy. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:390-395`, paper
    69	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1229-1421`. -/
    70	theorem exists_spcc_value_one (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    71	    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy (pauliBasisTestSymm P),
    72	      S.IsSPCC ∧ S.toStrategy.value = 1 := by
    73	  sorry
    74	
    75	end
    76	
    77	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions
+
+The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
+elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
+distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
+game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
+linear distributions rely on.
+-/
+
+/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
+weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
+`Distribution`. -/
+theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
+    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
+    μ = ν := by
+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl
+
+/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
+theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
+    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
+    rw [Finset.image_image]
+    rfl
+  · funext c
+    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
+        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
+      intro a ha
+      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
+      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
+    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
+    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
+        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
+      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
+    rw [← hkey]
+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
+    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
+    congr 1
+    ext a
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
+      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
+      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩
+
+/-- Every point of a finite type carries the same uniform weight.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
+  simp [uniformDistribution]
+
+/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
+distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
+    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
+    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
+  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
+    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
+    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
+      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
+    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
+    rwa [hc] at hpos
+  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
+    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
+      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
+      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
+    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
+    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
+    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
+    ext b
+    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
+    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
+      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
+      exact hcpos
+    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
+    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩
+  · funext b
+    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
+      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
+    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'
+    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b,
+        (uniformDistribution α).weight a) = (uniformDistribution β).weight b
+    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply α a,
+      uniformDistribution_weight_apply, Finset.sum_const, hc, nsmul_eq_mul, hcard]
+    push_cast
+    field_simp
+
+/-- Relabelling along a bijection preserves uniformity.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_equiv {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] (E : α ≃ β) :

+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ 1 fun b => ?_

+    ext a
+    simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
+  rw [hfilter]
+  simp
+
+/-- The first marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.fst = uniformDistribution α := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card β) fun a => ?_
+  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.1 = a)
+      = ({a} : Finset α) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset β) := by
+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton, and_true]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp
+
+/-- The second marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_snd {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.snd = uniformDistribution β := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card α) fun b => ?_
+  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.2 = b)
+      = (Finset.univ : Finset α) ×ˢ ({b} : Finset β) := by
+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp
+
+/-- Binding a uniform distribution to a family of uniformly seeded
+push-forwards is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on the product.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.bind`. -/
+theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (g : α → β → γ) :
+    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution α)

+      (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map fun p => g p.1 p.2 := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).biUnion

+      (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).image fun p => g p.1 p.2

+    simp [Prod.exists]
+  · funext c
+    have hcount :
+        ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c).card

+      simp only [Finset.card_filter]
+      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    have hinner : ∀ a : α,
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
+          = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *

+      intro a
+      change (∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c,

+      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply β b,

+      Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hcount, Fintype.card_prod]

   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the

   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}

   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level

   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level

   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.

   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}

   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding

   459	
   460	The question distributions of the classical low individual degree game and of
   461	the Pauli basis test (Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}) sample lines in $\F_q^m$;
   462	we record here the definition of lines and their canonical representatives.
   463	
   464	\begin{definition}[Lines]\label{def:line}
   465		A \emph{line} $\ell$ in $\F_q^m$ specified by a pair
   466		$(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$ is the subset
   467		\begin{equation}\label{eq:line-set}
   468			\ell(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m\;.
   469		\end{equation}
   470		The vector $v$ is called a \emph{direction} of $\ell(u,v)$; the case $v = 0$
   471		is explicitly allowed, in which case the line is the singleton $\{u\}$. A
   472		line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate
   473		$i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ for which $v = e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   474		vector of $\F_q^m$; such a line is said to be \emph{parallel to the $i$-th
   475		direction}. A line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists
   476		$i \in \{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ such that $v_1 = v_2 = \dots = v_i = 0$ (for
   477		$i = 0$ the condition is vacuous, so every line is diagonal).
   478	\end{definition}
   479	
   480	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:line-equiv}
   481		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePoints_eq_of_mem}
   482		\leanok
   483		\uses{def:line}
   484		Let $u, v \in \F_q^m$. Then for all $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, we have
   485		$\ell(u,v) = \ell(u',v)$.
   486	\end{proposition}
   487	\begin{proof}
   488		\leanok
   489		\uses{def:line}
   490		Fix $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, so $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$. Any
   491		$a \in \ell(u,v)$ has the form $a = u + sv = u' + (s - t)v$, so
   492		$\ell(u,v) \subseteq \ell(u',v)$. The symmetric argument gives the reverse
   493		inclusion.
   494	\end{proof}
   495	
   496	Thus, for a fixed direction, a line is an equivalence class of its points: the
   497	pair $(u,v)$ representing it can use any base point on the line. A canonical
   498	representation is obtained as follows.

   500	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]\label{def:line-representative}
   501		\uses{def:line, def:cl-canonical, prop:line-equiv}
   502		Let $\ell$ be a line in direction $v \neq 0$, and let
   503		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v : \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with
   504		the one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$
   505		(Definition~\ref{def:cl-canonical}). The \emph{canonical representative of
   506		$\ell$} is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   507		\[
   508			u_0 = L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u) \qquad \text{for all } u \in \ell\;.
   509		\]
   510		This is well defined: since the image and kernel of $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ are
   511		complementary, any $u \in \ell$ decomposes uniquely as $u = u_0 + tv$ with
   512		$u_0$ in the image, so $u_0 = u - tv \in \ell$ and
   513		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u_0) = u_0$; moreover any two points of $\ell$ differ by
   514		a multiple of $v$ and therefore have the same image under
   515		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$. A line $\ell = \ell(u,v)$ is henceforth canonically
   516		represented by the pair $(u_0, v)$. (For $v = 0$, where the singleton
   517		$\{u\}$ leaves no independent kernel basis, we take $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_0$ to
   518		be the identity---the canonical linear map with empty kernel basis---so
   519		that $u_0 = u$; the source leaves this case implicit.)
   520	\end{definition}

  1160	Conditionally linear functions specify the question distributions of the games considered in the following chapters in a form that can be ``introspected''.      1	\chapter{The Pauli basis test}
     2	\label{chap:qpbt-test}
     3	% Paper label sec:pauli-verifier kept for cross-reference fidelity; it resolves to this chapter.
     4	\label{sec:pauli-verifier}
     5	
     6	This chapter defines the two testing primitives underlying the question-reduction step: the \emph{classical low individual degree game}, in its simultaneous form, and the \emph{Pauli basis test}, a nonlocal game built from the classical game together with the Magic Square game. We state the quantum soundness of the classical game (Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, imported, with the facts required by the identification, which remain to be proved, recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; see Remark~\ref{rem:ld-soundness-provider}), the rigidity of the Magic Square game (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}, imported), completeness of the Pauli basis test (Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}), and the main soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test (Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}), whose proof occupies Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}--\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} and is completed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} only modulo the proof obligation documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. The chapter closes with the qubit form of the soundness statement (Corollary~\ref{cor:pauli-binary}) and the canonical parameter choice with its soundness bound (Definition~\ref{def:introparams}, Lemma~\ref{lem:delta-bound}).
     7	
     8	Throughout, the two players are denoted $\mathrm A$ and $\mathrm B$; for $w \in \{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}$ we write $\overline w$ for the other player. Games, strategies, values, conditionally linear (CL) functions and distributions, typed distributions sampled from the edges of a graph, and the state-dependent approximation $\approx_\delta$ between families of measurement operators are as in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-games}; the algebraic material on lines, canonical linear maps, the low-degree encoding, and generalized Pauli observables is from Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}.

    10	\section{The classical low individual degree game}
    11	% Paper labels sec:ld-verifier and sec:ld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
    12	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    13	\label{sec:ld-game}
    14	
    15	The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and

    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-520`;

    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators
    22	
    23	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    24	
    25	/--
    26	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    27	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`;
    28	paper origin
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    30	-/
    31	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    34	
    35	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    36	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`, paper origin
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    38	-/
    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    41	  Pi.single i 1
    42	
    43	/--
    44	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    45	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 464-478; paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    47	-/
    48	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=

    51	/--

    55	-/
    56	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    57	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0

    65	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :

   180	        if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0) =
   181	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
   182	          μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
   183	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   184	      intro a ha
   185	      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
   186	    _ = (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) /
   187	        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
   188	      rw [Finset.sum_div]
   189	    _ = 1 := div_self hpos.ne'
