   191	/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions
   192	
   193	The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
   194	elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
   195	distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
   196	game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
   197	linear distributions rely on.
   198	-/
   199	
   200	/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
   201	weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
   202	`Distribution`. -/
   203	theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
   204	    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
   205	    μ = ν := by
   206	  cases μ with
   207	  | mk s w hn ho =>
   208	    cases ν with
   209	    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
   210	      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
   211	      have hw : w = w' := hweight
   212	      subst hs
   213	      subst hw
   214	      rfl
   215	
   216	/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
   217	Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
   218	theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
   219	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   220	    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
   221	    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
   222	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   223	  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
   224	    rw [Finset.image_image]
   225	    rfl
   226	  · funext c
   227	    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
   228	        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
   229	      intro a ha
   230	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
   231	      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
   232	    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
   233	    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
   234	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
   235	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
   236	    rw [← hkey]
   237	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
   238	    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
   239	    congr 1
   240	    ext a
   241	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
   242	    constructor
   243	    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
   244	      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
   245	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
   246	      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩
   247	
   248	/-- Every point of a finite type carries the same uniform weight.
   249	Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   250	theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
   251	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
   252	    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
   253	  simp [uniformDistribution]
   254	
   255	/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
   256	distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
   257	auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   258	theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
   259	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   260	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
   261	    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
   262	    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
   263	    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
   264	  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
   265	    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
   266	    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
   267	      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
   268	    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
   269	    rwa [hc] at hpos
   270	  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
   271	    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
   272	      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
   273	      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
   274	    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
   275	    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
   276	    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
   277	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   278	  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
   279	    ext b
   280	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
   281	    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
   282	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
   283	      exact hcpos
   284	    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
   285	    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩
   286	  · funext b
   287	    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
   288	      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
   289	    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'
   290	    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b,
   291	        (uniformDistribution α).weight a) = (uniformDistribution β).weight b
   292	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply α a,
   293	      uniformDistribution_weight_apply, Finset.sum_const, hc, nsmul_eq_mul, hcard]
   294	    push_cast
   295	    field_simp
   296	
   297	/-- Relabelling along a bijection preserves uniformity.  Formalization-only
   298	auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   299	theorem uniformDistribution_map_equiv {α β : Type*}
   300	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   301	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] (E : α ≃ β) :
   302	    (uniformDistribution α).map E = uniformDistribution β := by
   303	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ 1 fun b => ?_
   304	  have hfilter :
   305	      ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => E a = b) = {E.symm b} := by
   306	    ext a
   307	    simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
   308	  rw [hfilter]
   309	  simp
   310	
   311	/-- The first marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
   312	Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   313	theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst {α β : Type*}
   314	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   315	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
   316	    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.fst = uniformDistribution α := by
   317	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card β) fun a => ?_
   318	  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.1 = a)
   319	      = ({a} : Finset α) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset β) := by
   320	    ext p
   321	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
   322	      Finset.mem_singleton, and_true]
   323	  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
   324	  simp
   325	
   326	/-- The second marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
   327	Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   328	theorem uniformDistribution_map_snd {α β : Type*}
   329	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   330	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
   331	    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.snd = uniformDistribution β := by
   332	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card α) fun b => ?_
   333	  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.2 = b)
   334	      = (Finset.univ : Finset α) ×ˢ ({b} : Finset β) := by
   335	    ext p
   336	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
   337	      Finset.mem_singleton]
   338	  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
   339	  simp
   340	
   341	/-- Binding a uniform distribution to a family of uniformly seeded
   342	push-forwards is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on the product.
   343	Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.bind`. -/
   344	theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
   345	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   346	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
   347	    (g : α → β → γ) :
   348	    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution α)
   349	        (fun a => (uniformDistribution β).map (g a)) =
   350	      (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map fun p => g p.1 p.2 := by
   351	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   352	  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).biUnion
   353	        (fun a => (Finset.univ : Finset β).image (g a)) =
   354	      (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).image fun p => g p.1 p.2
   355	    ext c
   356	    simp [Prod.exists]
   357	  · funext c
   358	    have hcount :
   359	        ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c).card
   360	          = ∑ a : α, ((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card := by
   361	      simp only [Finset.card_filter]
   362	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   363	    have hinner : ∀ a : α,
   364	        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
   365	          = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
   366	              (1 / (Fintype.card β : Error)) := by
   367	      intro a
   368	      change (∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c,
   369	          (uniformDistribution β).weight b) = _
   370	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply β b,
   371	        Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
   372	    have key : ∀ a : α, (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
   373	        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
   374	        = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
   375	            (1 / ((Fintype.card α : Error) * (Fintype.card β : Error))) := by
   376	      intro a
   377	      rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply, hinner a]
   378	      ring
   379	    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α), (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
   380	        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c) =
   381	      ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c,
   382	        (uniformDistribution (α × β)).weight p
   383	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a, ← Finset.sum_mul,
   384	      Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α × β) p,
   385	      Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hcount, Fintype.card_prod]
   386	    push_cast
   387	    ring

     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space, and their conditional-linearity levels are
    12	established below; the line-point distributions they induce are analysed in
    13	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    21	-/

    23	open scoped BigOperators

    31	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    32	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    34	`def:ld-game` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, with paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    37	-/
    38	structure LdParams where
    39	  q : ℕ
    40	  m : ℕ
    41	  d : ℕ
    42	  k : ℕ
    43	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    44	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    45	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    46	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    47	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    48	
    49	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    50	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    51	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    52	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    53	
    54	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    55	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    56	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    60	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    61	
    62	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    63	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    64	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    66	-/
    67	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    68	
    69	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    72	-/
    73	inductive LdType where
    74	  | point
    75	  | aline
    76	  | dline
    77	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    78	
    79	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    82	-/
    83	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    84	
    85	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

    90	
    91	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=

   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in

   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P

   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar

   194	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=

   197	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   198	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   199	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   200	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   201	  toFun x := fun i =>
   202	    match i with
   203	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   204	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   205	    | .inr _ => 0
   206	  map_add' x y := by
   207	    funext i
   208	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   209	  map_smul' c x := by
   210	    funext i
   211	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp

   213	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   214	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   215	other coordinate. -/
   216	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   217	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   218	  toFun x := fun i =>
   219	    match i with
   220	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   221	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   222	    | .inr _ => 0
   223	  map_add' x y := by
   224	    funext i
   225	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   226	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   227	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   228	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   229	      rfl
   230	    · simp
   231	    · simp
   232	  map_smul' c x := by
   233	    funext i
   234	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   235	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   237	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   238	      rfl
   239	    · simp
   240	    · simp

   242	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   243	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   244	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   245	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   246	  toFun x := fun k =>
   247	    match k with
   248	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   249	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   250	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   251	  map_add' x y := by
   252	    funext k
   253	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   254	    · simp
   255	    · simp
   256	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   257	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   258	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   259	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   260	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   261	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   262	        rfl
   263	  map_smul' c x := by
   264	    funext k
   265	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   266	    · simp
   267	    · simp
   268	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   269	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   270	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   271	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   272	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   273	        rfl

   362	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a two-level representation of the
   363	affine-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   364	private noncomputable def ldALineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   365	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 2 :=
   366	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   367	    fun y =>
   368	      .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   369	        (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y))))
   370	        (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   371	        fun _ => .zero

   373	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a three-level representation of the
   374	diagonal-line map as a conditionally linear function. -/
   375	private noncomputable def ldDLineTerm (P : LdParams) :
   376	    CondLinearTerm (ScalarQ P) (ι := LdIndex P) 3 :=
   377	  .succ (ldSeedRegister P) (ldSeedLinear P) (ldSeedLinear_supported P)
   378	    fun y =>
   379	      .succ (ldDirectionRegister P)
   380	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))
   381	        (ldDirectionCLLinear_supported P _)
   382	        fun w =>
   383	          .succ (ldPointRegister P)
   384	            (ldPointCLLinear P (LdSpace.direction w))
   385	            (ldPointCLLinear_supported P _)
   386	            fun _ => .zero

   388	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is
   389	`lem:ld-aline-level`, the level-2 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   390	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:61-71`, paper
   391	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   392	-/
   393	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   394	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   395	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   396	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   397	  funext x
   398	  have hseed :
   399	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   400	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   401	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   402	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   403	  have hval :
   404	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   405	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   406	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   407	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   408	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   409	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   410	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   411	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   412	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   413	    rw [hseed]
   414	  rw [hval]
   415	  funext i
   416	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   417	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   418	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   419	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   420	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   421	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   422	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   423	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   424	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   425	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   426	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   427	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]
   428	
   429	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is
   430	`lem:ld-dline-level`, the level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   431	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:73-83`, paper origin
   432	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   433	-/
   434	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   435	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   436	  refine ⟨ldDLineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   437	    ⟨ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ =>
   438	      ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   439	  funext x
   440	  have hseed :
   441	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   442	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   443	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   444	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   445	  have hdir :
   446	      LdSpace.direction
   447	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   448	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) =
   449	        prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) := by
   450	    funext j
   451	    change prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   452	        (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j = _
   453	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction]
   454	  have hval :
   455	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldDLineTerm P) x =
   456	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   457	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   458	              (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   459	            (ldPointCLLinear P
   460	                (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   461	                (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) := by
   462	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   463	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   464	            (chiIndex P
   465	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   466	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   467	          (ldPointCLLinear P
   468	              (LdSpace.direction
   469	                (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   470	                  (chiIndex P
   471	                    (LdSpace.seed
   472	                      (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   473	                  (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)))
   474	              (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) = _
   475	    rw [hseed, hdir]
   476	  rw [hval]
   477	  funext i
   478	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   479	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) +
   480	        (lineRepMap
   481	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   482	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0)) =
   483	      lineRepMap (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   484	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   485	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, zero_add, add_zero]
   486	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   487	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   488	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero]
   489	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   490	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   491	            (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j +
   492	          ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) =
   493	      prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) j
   494	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction, zero_add, add_zero, add_zero]

   502	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in

   513	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   514	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   515	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   516	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`; paper
   517	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   518	-/
   519	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   520	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   521	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   522	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   523	  deriving DecidableEq
   524	
   525	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   526	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   527	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   528	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   529	-/
   530	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   531	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   532	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   533	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   534	
   535	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   536	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   537	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   538	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   539	-/
   540	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   541	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   542	  toFun
   543	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   544	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   545	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   546	  invFun
   547	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   548	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   549	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   550	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   551	  right_inv := by
   552	    intro x
   553	    cases x with
   554	    | inl a => rfl
   555	    | inr x =>
   556	        cases x with
   557	        | inl a => rfl
   558	        | inr a => rfl

   560	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   561	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   562	
   563	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   564	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   565	
   566	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   567	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   568	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   569	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   570	-/
   571	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   572	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   573	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   574	
   575	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   576	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   577	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   578	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   579	-/
   580	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   581	  match t, a with
   582	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   583	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   584	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   585	  | _, _ => false
   586	
   587	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   588	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   589	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   590	-/
   591	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   592	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   593	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   594	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   595	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   596	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   597	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   598	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   599	
   600	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   601	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   602	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   603	-/
   604	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   605	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   606	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   607	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   608	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   609	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   610	
   611	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   612	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   613	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   614	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   615	-/
   616	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   617	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   618	  open Classical in
   619	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   620	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   621	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   622	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   623	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   624	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   625	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   626	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   627	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   628	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   629	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   630	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)

   632	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)

    36	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
    37	vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
    38	private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    39	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    40	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    41	  invFun p := fun i =>
    42	    match i with
    43	    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
    44	    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
    45	    | .inr j => p.2 j

    47	    funext i
    48	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
    49	    · rfl
    50	    · cases u
    51	      rfl
    52	    · rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by
    54	    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
    55	    rfl

   107	private theorem chiIndex_eq_iff (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) (i : Fin L.m) :
   108	    chiIndex L s = i ↔

   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
   133	  have hstep2 :
   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,
   182	    ← hstep2, hstep3, Nat.card_Ico]
   183	  omega

   374	/-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite

   376	noncomputable abbrev PolyIndex (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   377	    [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)
   378	
   379	/-- A POVM indexed by one bounded multivariate polynomial. -/
   380	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   381	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   382	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] := Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι
   383	
   384	/-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may
   385	have its own coefficient field, number of variables, and degree bound.
   386	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:164-171`, paper
   387	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   388	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
   389	    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
   390	    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   391	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   392	  Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
   393	
   394	/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
   395	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   396	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
   397	
   398	/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   399	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   400	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   401	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
   402	
   403	/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   404	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   405	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   406	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   407	
   408	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   409	point question. -/
   410	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   411	  fun i => match i with
   412	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   413	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   414	  | .inr _ => 0
   415	
   416	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   417	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   418	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   419	
   420	/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
   421	wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
   422	answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   423	def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
   424	  | .pointVals values => values
   425	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   426	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   427	
   428	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   429	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   430	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   431	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   432	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   433	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   434	
   435	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   436	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
   437	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
   438	
   439	The first two consistency bounds compare the point-answer postprocessing of the
   440	strategy with evaluations of the polynomial measurements. Answers of the wrong
   441	form are folded into the zero tuple so that the point family remains a POVM.
   442	
   443	The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
   444	and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
   445	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
   446	`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
   447	theorem exists_ld_soundness :
   448	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   449	      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   450	        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   451	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
   452	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   453	                (fun u outcome =>
   454	                  heteroKron
   455	                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   456	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
   457	                (fun u outcome =>
   458	                  heteroKron 1
   459	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   460	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   461	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   462	                (fun u outcome =>
   463	                  heteroKron
   464	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   465	                (fun u outcome =>
   466	                  heteroKron 1
   467	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   468	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
   469	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   470	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   471	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   472	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   473	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
   474	  sorry
   475	
   476	end
   477	
   478	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

--- paper CL funcs ---
     1	\section{Conditionally Linear Functions, Distributions, and Samplers}
     2	\label{sec:linear}
     3	
     4	\subsection{Conditionally linear functions and distributions}
     5	\label{sec:cl}
     6	
     7	We first introduce \emph{conditionally linear functions}, which are used to
     8	specify the question distribution for games considered in the paper in a way
     9	that the question distribution can be ``introspected'', as described in
    10	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}.
    11	Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element
    12	$x\in V = \F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$, and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially
    13	on $x^{V_j}$ where $V_1,V_2,\ldots $ are a sequence of complementary register
    14	subspaces such that both the linear maps $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$ for
    15	$j \ge 2$ may depend on the values taken by previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$,
    16	$L_2(x^{V_2})$, etc.
    17	
    18	In the remainder of the section we use $V$ to denote the linear space $\F^n$ for
    19	some integer $n \geq 0$.
    20	For ease of notation we extensively use the subscript range notation.
    21	For example, if $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \in
    22	\{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ we write
    23	\begin{equation*}
    24	  V_{<k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\,1 \le j<k} V_j\;,\quad
    25	  V_{> k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\, \ell\ge j > k} V_j\;,
    26	\end{equation*}
    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}
    86	
    87	\begin{figure}[!htbp]
    88	  \centering
    89	  \begin{tikzpicture}
    90	
    91	
    92	
    93	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=east] at (0,0) (xv1) {$x^{V_{1}}$};
    94	    \node[draw, minimum width=6cm, anchor=west] at (-.4pt,0) {$x^{V_{>1}}$};
    95	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=east] at (0,-2) (xl1) {$x^{L_{1}}$};
    96	    \draw[-stealth] (xv1.south) -- ++(0,-1) node[above right] {$L_{1}$} -- (xl1.north);
    97	
    98	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=west] at (0,-3) (xv2) {$x^{V_{2}}$};
    99	    \node[draw, minimum width=4cm, anchor=west] at (2cm,-3) {$x^{V_{>2}}$};
   100	
   101	    \node[draw, minimum width=2cm, anchor=west] at (0,-5) (xl2) {$x^{L_{2}}$};
   102	
   103	    \draw[-stealth] (xv2.south) -- ++(0,-1) node[above right]
   104	      {$L_{2,\,x^{{L_{1}}}}$} -- (xl2.north);
   105	    \draw[dashed, -stealth, to path={|- (\tikztotarget)}] (xl1) edge (xv2.west);
   106	
   107	    \draw[dashed, -stealth, to path={|- (\tikztotarget)}] (xl2) edge (3cm,-6);
   108	    \draw[dashed, -stealth, to path={|- (\tikztotarget)}] (xl1) edge (3cm,-6);
   109	    \node[right] at (3cm,-6) {$\;\cdots\cdots$};
   110	
   111	  \end{tikzpicture}
   112	  \caption{An illustration of an $\ell$-level CL function $L$.
   113	    First a register subspace $V_{1}$ and a linear map $L_{1}$ are chosen and
   114	    applied to obtain $x^{L_{1}} = L_{1}(x^{V_{1}}) \in V_{1}$.
   115	    Then depending the value of $x^{L_{1}}$, a register subspace $V_{2}$ and a
   116	    linear map $L_{2,\,x^{L_{1}}}$ are chosen and applied to obtain
   117	    $x^{L_{2}} = L_{2,\,x^{{L_{1}}}}(x^{V_{2}}) \in V_{2}$ and so on.
   118	    Finally, $L(x)$ is defiend to be
   119	    $\sum_{k=1}^{\ell} x^{L_{k}}$.}\label{fig:cl-functions}
   120	\end{figure}
   121	
   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,
   128	  $L_1(x)=0$ for all $x\in V$, and $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is the $0$ map for all
   129	  $x\in V$.
   130	\end{remark}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}

   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.

   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}

   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,

  1330	% Paper section label sec:types kept for cross-reference fidelity. Only the mathematical

  1334	\label{sec:types}
  1335	
  1336	The question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.
  1337	
  1338	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]\label{def:typed-cl-functions}
  1339		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsTypedCondLinearFamily}
  1340		\leanok
  1341		\uses{def:cl-func}
  1342		Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite set (the \emph{type set}) and let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \ge 0$. A \emph{$\mathcal T$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_t\}_{t \in \mathcal T}$ such that, for each $t \in \mathcal T$, $L_t$ is an $\ell$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.
  1343	\end{definition}
  1344	
  1345	% Nonemptiness of the edge set is stated explicitly here: with E empty, m = k = 0 and the
  1346	% normalization 1/(2m-k) below is undefined. The source
  1347	% (references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82) leaves this boundary hypothesis implicit.
  1348	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]\label{def:graph-distribution}
  1349		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.graphDistribution}
  1350		\leanok
  1351		Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and nonempty edge set $E$. Edges in $E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u = v$ represents a self-loop. Suppose there are $m \ge 1$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops. Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of $G$} is the distribution over $U \times U$ such that for every $(u,v) \in U \times U$,
  1352		\[
  1353			\mu_G(u, v) =
  1354			\begin{cases}
  1355				1/(2m-k) & \text{if } \{u,v\} \in E\,,\\
  1356				0 & \text{otherwise}\,.
  1357			\end{cases}
  1358		\]
  1359		This is identical to the uniform distribution over ordered pairs $(u,v) \in U \times U$ such that $\{u,v\} \in E$: each edge that is not a self-loop contributes two ordered pairs, and each self-loop contributes one, whence the normalization $2m-k$.
  1360	\end{definition}

  1363		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.graphDistribution_isProbability}
  1364		\leanok
  1365		\uses{def:graph-distribution}
  1366		This is not a named statement of the source article; it records the normalization of the graph distribution of Definition~\ref{def:graph-distribution}, which the source leaves implicit. Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with nonempty edge set $E$. Then the graph distribution $\mu_G$ has total mass one, that is, $\sum_{(u,v) \in U \times U} \mu_G(u,v) = 1$.
  1367	\end{lemma}
  1368	\begin{proof}
  1369		\leanok
  1370		\uses{def:graph-distribution}

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.CondLinear
